concept.title: Headings
concept.abstract: This section covers the Heading style in Markdown — its role as the primary structural mechanism that organizes a document's content into a named, hierarchical sequence of sections — and four scenarios: headings applied in correct sequential order, a heading level skipped in the hierarchy, a top-level heading absent from the document, and consecutive headings with no body content between them. The converter reads each heading level to construct the DITA map hierarchy, generating sub-maps, topic files, and topic type classifications from the heading sequence and the content that follows each heading.

conbody.p: A Heading style marks the beginning of a named section of content and assigns it a rank in the document hierarchy. It is the primary structural mechanism of any technical document — headings divide continuous content into discrete, named units, establish the parent-child relationships between those units, and create the navigational backbone that readers and publishing systems depend on.

The heading hierarchy is expressed through levels: a top-level heading (Heading 1) names a major section; each lower-level heading (Heading 2 through Heading N) names a subsection within its parent. This ranked sequence carries the same structural meaning regardless of the format it is expressed. The level communicates the section's position in the hierarchy; the text communicates its subject.
conbody.note: Only a semantically marked heading — applied through the document's native heading mechanism — creates a genuine section boundary that a converter, search engine, or publishing system can detect and act on.
conbody.p: In a .docx file, the built-in Heading styles are paragraph styles — Heading 1 through Heading N — each carrying an outline level attribute. The outline level is a zero-indexed integer: Heading 1 carries outline level 0, Heading 2 carries outline level 1, and so on.
conbody.note: The DITA-XML converter reads the heading outline levels in sequence and uses them to construct the root DITA map tree. The heading 1 or outline level 0 is used to create sub ditamaps <mapref> nested in the root DITA map. The subsequent outline level 2 to N generates nested topic files <topicref> . And the content between one heading and the next becomes a single .dita topic file (concept, task, reference and so on).
conbody.p: The sub Ditamap and respective topics is organized in the sequential order to establish the parent-child map relationships between topics, and create the navigational backbone in the published output such as PDF or Online document.

ul.li: A gap in the heading sequence — for example, a Heading 3 appearing directly under a Heading 1 with no Heading 2 between them — causes the converter to promote the lower-level heading. Heading 4 (####) and deeper levels should be used sparingly because they are converted to paragraph content rather than additional structural levels.
A multi-level heading sequence with empty paragraphs (no context) will generate empty DITA topics or map to <topichead> - altering the intended hierarchy in the output.

conbody.p: In Markdown, headings are created by placing one or more hash (#) characters at the beginning of a line. In most projects, the converter supports three effective heading levels per topic.

The converter analyzes the heading hierarchy within each Markdown file to determine how the content is organized in the generated DITA topic. If title metadata is not available, Heading 1 (#) becomes the topic title. Heading 2 (##) becomes a section title or, in a task topic, a subtopic under the parent topic. Heading 3 (###) and lower heading levels are converted to paragraph content.
conbody.note: Do not use bold text (**Heading**) in place of a Markdown heading (# Heading). Bold formatting has no structural meaning. The converter treats it as paragraph content and appends the following content to the current topic instead of creating a new topic.
conbody.p: The following table shows how each Markdown heading level maps to a DITA construct.

row.entry: If there is no title metadata, the H1 (#) becomes the title of the topic.
The H2 (##) becomes the title of the section of the topic. In case of a task topic, it becomes a subtopic under the parent topic.
The H3 (###) becomes a paragraph tag.
The H4 (####) becomes a paragraph tag.
The H5 (#####) becomes a paragraph tag.

conbody.note: Begin each Markdown topic with a Heading 1 ( # ) and use heading levels sequentially without skipping intermediate levels. Use headings to represent the logical structure of the document rather than to achieve a particular visual appearance. This helps the converter preserve the intended hierarchy without applying fallback promotion rules.
